summary.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA positive at INR 174 mn (5.9% margin) and PAT INR 44 mn; FY26 EBITDA still negative INR 52 mn after heavy reinvestment.
summary.overview: MobiKwik reported back-to-back EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarters in Q3 and Q4 FY26, with Q4 total income of INR 2,960 mn (+6% YoY) and contribution margin of 46% versus 23% a year earlier. FY26 EBITDA improved to negative INR 52 mn from negative INR 794 mn, and full-year PAT narrowed to negative INR 621 mn from negative INR 1,215 mn. Management said it is deliberately reinvesting core payments and lending profits (about INR 55 crore spent in FY26) into four growth engines: offline and online merchant payments, an NBFC, and AI. Analysts pressed on the gap between UPI-led GMV growth and flat payments revenue, on the timing of breakeven for merchant businesses, and on NBFC rollout.

segments.name: Payments (wallet, UPI, recharge and bill payments)
segments.commentary: Wallet is the largest in India by GTV with about 20% share as of March 2026. Customer-initiated UPI transactions grew 170% YoY vs industry 26%. Recharge and bill payments GMV reached INR 269 bn in FY26 (2.2x). Payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters as UPI mix rises and gross take rate falls.

segments.name: Lending (digital credit, LSP model)
segments.commentary: Management cited a 59% gross margin in Q4, with super-prime share of disbursements up from 10% to 32% and repeat loans up from 20% to 63.5%. Lending spread was 5.3% (analyst cited 5.4%); management sees 4.5% as more sustainable, with 4% as the sweet spot. FY26 digital credit GMV was about INR 3,200 crore.

segments.name: Merchant payments (offline and Zaakpay online)
segments.commentary: Offline targets 5x device scale-up for 10x revenue by FY28; Zaakpay targets 10x GMV by FY28. Both are guided to reach EBITDA breakeven by FY28. Merchant partners stand at 4.9 mn.

guidance_outlook: GMV growth of 30-35% expected in both payments and lending in FY27 (per management).
Digital credit GMV growth of 30-35% in FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided in the same broad range as the current ~5%, with better unit margins offset by higher investment.
Merchant-business investment of roughly INR 55 crore in FY26 expected to be similar in FY27; investment to continue for at least 18 months.
Fixed costs at INR 115-120 crore per quarter; 15-20% increase expected in FY27 from depreciation and device-distribution people costs.
Payments margin guided at 12-15 bps mid-to-long term; management advised against modelling 16 bps over two years.
NBFC timeline: move LSP business into a wholly owned subsidiary in 2-3 months, set up NBFC in 3-6 months, launch co-lending disbursals in 6-9 months.
Target of 10-20% of the market leader's size in offline merchant categories in 18-24 months; Zaakpay 10x GMV in about 18-24 months.
Management expects payments revenue to follow GMV growth from the next few quarters once PPI-over-UPI MDR is implemented.
capex_capacity: Merchant device investment is capitalised and depreciated; other merchant spend (people, product) is expensed through P&L. INR 55 crore total FY26 investment excludes device capex.
Depreciation rising as merchant devices are deployed.
Part of unencumbered cash is still IPO proceeds not yet available, which trickle in as used; IPO funds also being used for merchant investment and will hit P&L.
NBFC to be funded by parent capital infusion into the wholly owned NBFC subsidiary, subject to board and shareholder approval.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue flat for 4-5 quarters despite GMV growth: UPI mix dilutes gross take rate, and some low-margin categories were added.
PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet been implemented; management expects it to add revenue.
UPI credit and RuPay credit transactions generate MDR; plain bank UPI does not.
Net payments margin remains positive; gross take rate has moderated in existing businesses.
Lending: digital credit GMV growth was subdued QoQ as the company prioritised quality over volume.
Offline merchant focus on three categories: organised retail (mid-market and above), petrol and oil/gas, and small mom-and-pop stores. Zaakpay targets education, government and BBPS categories.

qa_highlights.question: What is being done to fix payments revenue growth, and is there long-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue lags GMV because growth is UPI-led and PPI-over-UPI MDR has not yet come; consistent revenue growth is expected in the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much investment is needed in the merchant business over two years, and is it through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 55 crore was invested in FY26, and a similar range is expected in FY27. Everything except device capitalisation hits P&L, and IPO proceeds are being used for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the merchant breakeven timeline move from 3-4 quarters to FY28, and what does baseline profitability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs were raised deliberately to build new businesses; without the merchant investment FY26 EBITDA would have been about INR 50 crore. Management aims to stay PAT-positive while reinvesting, with FY27 EBITDA hypothetically between 1x and 2x of the reinvested base.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ex-UPI GTV growing above 30% while payments revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited gross take rate moderation and mix shift to lower-margin categories; the non-UPI revenue growth has been below expectations.

qa_highlights.question: What are the NBFC timelines and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: LSP business moves to a subsidiary in 2-3 months, NBFC set up in 3-6 months, and co-lending disbursals launch in 6-9 months. Parent will infuse capital after board and shareholder approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital debt still INR 261 crore when cash is INR 434 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the cash is still IPO proceeds not yet accessible; the short-term lines cover weekend and holiday settlement gaps when bank funds are delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% lending margin sustainable and what is the payments margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers 4.5% as more sustainable and 4% as the sweet spot, and guided 12-15 bps for payments mid-to-long term, though Q4 ran above that.

qa_highlights.question: What fixed-cost increase is expected next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs are INR 115-120 crore per quarter; a 15-20% increase is expected in FY27.

risks_watch: Payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters even as GMV rises; PPI-over-UPI MDR timing is uncertain.
Gross take-rate compression from UPI mix and low-margin categories.
Merchant investment of about INR 55 crore a year continues for at least 18 months, delaying group profitability; FY28 breakeven target for the merchant businesses.
FLDG capital is blocked against lending book growth and absorbs about 5% of credit cost.
Lending margin of 5.3% may normalise toward 4-4.5%; some gains came from previously matured cohorts.
Regulatory risk on payments MDR and on the NBFC licence and governance.
Working capital dependence (INR 261 crore) and finance cost reduction; IPO proceeds still being drawn down.
Merchant partner growth was only about 7% last year, with a more aggressive onboarding target not yet quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the profitability turnaround and growth-engine narrative, but noticeably evasive on payments revenue growth, the rationale for the merchant-breakeven timeline, and NBFC scale. Management repeatedly deferred numeric detail to later quarters and hedged the lending margin and the 16 bps payments guidance.
key_quotes: We ended the year with back-to-back profitable quarters.
In payments, revenue generally follows GMV.
But I don't think from a 2-year time frame I would recommend modeling for 16 basis points because we really can't tell if and when any regulatory change could change that.

adds.what: Offline merchant device scale-up (5x devices targeted for 10x revenue by FY28)

growth.why: Management guides 30-35% GMV growth in payments and digital credit for FY27 and a 15-20% rise in fixed costs, backed by stated market share (~20% wallet GTV), device scale-up targets and an NBFC timeline, but no hard capacity or contracted orders are quantified and payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters.
